Course CYL101: Environmental Science. Offered by Chemistry. Credits: 1.0. Load (L-T-P): 1-0-0. Typically offered in semester 1. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course MEP102: Digital fabrication. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 1-0.5-3. Typically offered in semester 2. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture-lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: CAD modelling (working); Additive manufacturing (working); Engineering drawing (working); Machining and metal cutting (intro).

MEP102 Digital fabrication — syllabus: Theory of projections; Orthographic projection; Isometric projection and perspective projection; Familiarization with 3D solid modelling (CAD) for the creation of engineering and freeform geometries; 3D Scanning using CMM and laser scanners and their applications and Preparatory activities for 3D Printing: Conversion of CAD model into a real part, stl format ant its importance, slicing, effect of part orientation; 3D printing of the part: Introduction to additive manufacturing process; conventional machining processes: turning, centering, drilling, and milling; CNC programming, Familiarization with machining processes using tabletop reconfigurable CNC machines; Familiarization with Casting, Welding, and molding and its inspection; Laser-based manufacturing processes (Demonstration of Laser cutting machine); Introduction to the concept of Digital manufacturing and industry 4.0

Course EEL101: Basic Electrical Engineering. Offered by Electrical Engineering. Credits: 4.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-2. Typically offered in semester 2. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture-lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course ECL101: Basic Electronics Engineering. Offered by Electrical Engineering. Credits: 4.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-2. Typically offered in semester 2. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture-lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course BML101: Biology for Engineers. Offered by Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Typically offered in semester 2. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course LAL100: Introduction to Communication Skills. Offered by Liberal Arts. Credits: 2.0. Load (L-T-P): 1-1-0. Typically offered in semester 3. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course LAL101: Introduction to Finance. Offered by Liberal Arts. Credits: 1.0. Load (L-T-P): 1-0-0. Typically offered in semester 4. Course type: institute-core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course MML204: Phases, Phase Transformations and Properties of Materials. Offered by Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Typically offered in semester 3. Course type: core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Phase diagrams and transformations (working); Materials science (working).

Course EEL208: Sensors & Instrumentation. Offered by Electrical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Typically offered in semester 6. Course type: core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Metrology and measurement (working).

Course MEL231: Engineering Mechanics. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 2-1-0. Typically offered in semester 3. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Statics and equilibrium (advanced); Free body diagrams (working); Truss and frame analysis (working); Friction and its applications (working); Rigid body dynamics (working).

MEL231 Engineering Mechanics — syllabus: Introduction: Mechanics - Method of Solving Problems - Forces and Force Equilibrium in Plane and Space; Rigid Bodies: Equivalent systems of Forces - Forces and Moments - Couple - Equilibrium in two and three dimensions; Distributed Forces: Center of Gravity and Centroids of Planes and Volumes - Moments of Inertia of Area, Parallel-axis Theorem; Analysis of Structures: Trusses and Frames - Internal forces in members - Beams - Shear Force - Bending Moment; Friction: Wedge, Screws, Belt Friction; Method of Virtual Work: Principle of Virtual Work and its application to solve problems of mechanics; Rigid-body kinematics: Absolute motion - Relative velocity - Relative acceleration - Rotation relative to rotating axes; Rigid-body kinetics: Linear Momentum - Angular momentum - Kinetic energy - Work and energy - Impulse and momentum; Rigid body in three-dimensions: Kinematics - Kinetics - Gyroscopes.

Course MEL211: Thermodynamics. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 2-1-0. Typically offered in semester 3. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Laws of thermodynamics (advanced); Properties of pure substances (working); Power and refrigeration cycles (intro).

MEL211 Thermodynamics — syllabus: Introductory concepts and definitions: Macroscopic and microscopic point of view, system, surroundings, boundary, thermodynamics properties, thermodynamics state and equilibrium, steady state, work interaction, various forms of work; First law of thermodynamics: Quasi-static and reversible processes; Heat interaction; Adiabatic process; Zeroth law of thermodynamics, temperature, Celsius scale of temperature, ideal gas scales of temperature, properties of fluids, internal energy, enthalpy, Carnot cycle; First law analysis for a control volume/open system, steady-state and transient processes with engineering applications; Second law of thermodynamics: Kelvin-Planck's statement, Clausius Statement and corollaries, Heat engines and refrigerators, absolute temperature scale, Second law analysis for a control volume/open system; Entropy and the Clausius inequality:

MEL211 Thermodynamics — syllabus: engines and refrigerators, absolute temperature scale, Second law analysis for a control volume/open system; Entropy and the Clausius inequality: Second law in terms of entropy, adiabatic-reversible-isentropic processes, entropy generation, the Gibbs equation, entropy for ideal gases, entropy change for reversible and irreversible processes, concepts of availability and exergy analysis for closed and open systems; Properties of Substances: Properties of pure substances - phase equilibrium diagrams p-v, p-T, T-s and h-s planes; dryness fraction, steam tables and Mollier diagram; Thermodynamics property relations: Maxwells relations, TdS relations, ratio of heat capacities.

Course MEL251: Casting, Forming and Welding. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Typically offered in semester 3. Course type: core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Casting processes (advanced); Welding and joining (advanced); Metal forming (working); Manufacturing and materials (working).

MEL251 Casting, Forming and Welding — syllabus: Basics of manufacturing, Primary and secondary manufacturing and its types, brief overview of metals; Casting: Introduction to casting, types of patterns and its allowance, types of moulding materials, gating system and its design, riser design, types of casting such as ingot/continuous and shape casting (investment casting, die casting, sand casting, centrifugal casting etc.), casting defect, casting solidification for pure metal and alloy; Welding: Fundamentals of welding and its types, Gas welding/Cutting, Arc welding (TIG, MIG, SAW etc.), Arc characteristics, modes of metal transfer, types of power source and its characteristics, Spot welding, Brazing, soldering, Solid state welding; Forming: Stress-strain curve, Yield function, Various types of bulk forming process such as rolling, extrusion, forging, wire drawing and its force analysis, sheet metal forming such as blanking, punching, deep drawing etc. Forming defects; Introduction to powder metallurgy: Basic definition, process, application.

Course MEL232: Mechanics of Solids. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 2-1-0. Typically offered in semester 4. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Stress and strain analysis (advanced); Beam bending and torsion (advanced); Failure theories and fatigue (working); Mechanical properties of materials (working).

MEL232 Mechanics of Solids — syllabus: Introduction: Deformable bodies - Analysis of deformable bodies - Solution of some statically indeterminate problems; Stress: Introduction to stress, Plane stress, Equilibrium equations - Stress transformation in plane stress - Mohr's Circle - Thin cylinders; Strain: Introduction to deformation and strain - Plane strain - Strain transformation - Measurement of strains using strain Gauge and strain rosette; Stress-strain relationship: Tension and compression test of metallic bars - Hooke's law for uniaxial and multi-axial loading - Thermal strains - Equations of elasticity, Introduction of Fatigue behavior and S-N curve - Theories of Failure - Stress concentration; Torsion: Torsion of circular shafts - Torsion of elastic hollow shaft - Introduction to torsion of rectangular shafts - Torsion of thin-walled shafts; Bending: Pure bending of beams - Moment-Curvature relationship - Stress-strain relation in bending - Elastic beams with transverse forces - Transverse shear stresses - Built-up beams - Composite beams; Deflection of beams:

MEL232 Mechanics of Solids — syllabus: relation in bending - Elastic beams with transverse forces - Transverse shear stresses - Built-up beams - Composite beams; Deflection of beams: Governing equation - Deflection using the moment of integration - Method of superposition - Energy methods - Castigliano's theorem; Buckling of Columns: Stability of equilibrium - Elastic instability of flexible columns - Critical loads for different boundary conditions of columns.

Course MEL214: Applied Thermal Engineering. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 2-1-0. Typically offered in semester 4. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Power and refrigeration cycles (advanced); Combustion and IC engines (working); Psychrometry and air conditioning (intro).

MEL214 Applied Thermal Engineering — syllabus: Introduction to Various Thermodynamics Systems: Simple Steam Power Plant, Gas Turbines, Internal Combustion Engines, Domestic Refrigerators, Air Conditioners, Jet Propulsion, Rocket Propulsion, Gas Compressors; Vapor Power Cycles: Actual vapor power cycle processes, Rankine and Carnot Cycles, Mean temperature of heat addition, Reheating cycle, Regenerative Cycles, Reheat-Regenerative Cycles, Exergy Analysis of Vapor Power Cycles, Binary Vapor Power Cycles; Gas Power Cycles: Carnot cycles, Stirling Cycles, Ericsson Cycles, Air Standard Cycles, Otto Cycles, Diesel Cycle, Dual Cycles, Comparison of Otto, Diesel and Dual Cycles, Lenoir Cycle, Atkinson Cycle, Brayton Cycles, Aircraft Propulsion; Cogeneration and Combined Cycles: Combined gas-steam power Plant, Different arrangements in combined cycles; Basics of Refrigeration Cycles: Reversed Heat Engines Cycles, Vapor Compression Refrigeration Cycles, Gas Cycle Refrigeration; Gas Compressors:

MEL214 Applied Thermal Engineering — syllabus: Basics of Refrigeration Cycles: Reversed Heat Engines Cycles, Vapor Compression Refrigeration Cycles, Gas Cycle Refrigeration; Gas Compressors: Compression Processes, Work of Compression, Reciprocating compressors, Single-Stage Reciprocating Air Compressors, Volumetric Efficiency, Multistage Compression.

Course MEL212: Fluid Mechanics. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 4.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-1-0. Typically offered in semester 4. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Fluid statics and manometry (working); Viscous flow and boundary layers (advanced); Compressible flow (intro).

MEL212 Fluid Mechanics — syllabus: Introduction: Basic ideas of continuum, fluid properties including viscosity, surface tension and vapour pressure; Fluid Statics: Hydrostatic pressure distribution, Manometry, Forces on submerged bodies, Buoyancy and Floatation, Stability of floating bodies, Pressure distribution in rigid body motion; Fluid Kinematics: Lagrangian and Eulerian descriptions, Deformation of fluid element, Strain rates, Vorticity, Flow description using pathline, streamline and streak line; Conservation laws: Reynolds Transport Theorem, Integral form of conservation laws - mass, linear momentum, angular momentum and energy, Differential form of conservation laws, Elementary derivation of Navier-Stokes equations, Exact solution to Navier-Stokes equations: Couette flow and Poiseulle flow etc.; Inviscid flows: Bernoulli equation and applications, overview of various losses; Plane potential flows: Streamfunction-velocity potential, superposition, source, sink, Doublet, flow past a cylinder, circulation, D'Alembert's Paradox; Dimensional analysis:

MEL212 Fluid Mechanics — syllabus: potential, superposition, source, sink, Doublet, flow past a cylinder, circulation, D'Alembert's Paradox; Dimensional analysis: Buckingham Pi theorem, dimensionless groups, similitude laws and scaling, practical applications; Boundary Layer Theory: Definition of boundary layer thickness, momentum thickness and energy thickness, Blasius solution, Von-Karman Momentum integral equation; Introduction to Turbulent flows: Basic definition and characteristics of turbulent flow, Energy Cascade, Mean and Fluctuating Components, Derivations of Reynolds Averaged Navier-Stokes Equations, Turbulent Flow through a Pipe and Channel, Moody Diagram, Hydrodynamic Smooth and Rough Pipe and Example Problems; Introduction to Compressible flows: High speed gas flow, speed of sound, One-dimensional form of the governing equations, Isentropic gas relations, Velocity measurement using a pitot tube at all Mach numbers.

Course MEL252: Fundamentals of Industrial Engineering. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Typically offered in semester 4. Course type: core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Operations and production planning (advanced); Optimisation (working); Industrial engineering (advanced).

MEL252 Fundamentals of Industrial Engineering — syllabus: Production Planning and Control: Forecasting models, aggregate production planning, scheduling, Lean manufacturing, Concurrent engineering, materials requirement planning and inventory management; Operations Research: Linear programming, simplex method etc., Transportation and Assignment Problems, network flow models, simple queuing models, PERT and CPM; TQM: Introduction, Historical Review, TQM Principles: six sigma, Kaizen etc., Quality Function Deployment (QFD), Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), FMEA, Quality Systems: Need for ISO 9000 and ISO 14000 - Concept, Requirements and Benefits, Case Studies.

Course MEL333: Design of Machine Elements. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.5. Load (L-T-P): 3-0.5-0. Typically offered in semester 5. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Machine element design (advanced); Failure theories and fatigue (advanced).

MEL333 Design of Machine Elements — syllabus: Basics: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering Design, Engineering Materials - Load and Stress Analysis, Deflection and Stiffness; Failure Prevention: Failure resulting from static loading; Fatigue failure resulting from variable loading; Design of Mechanical elements: Shafts; Power Screw, Threaded Joints, Bolt, Rivet, Weld; Springs; Bearings; Gears; Clutch, Break, Belts.

Course MEL313: Heat and Mass Transfer. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.5. Load (L-T-P): 3-0.5-0. Typically offered in semester 5. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Conduction (advanced); Convection (working); Radiation (working); Heat exchangers (working); Mass transfer (intro).

MEL313 Heat and Mass Transfer — syllabus: Introduction: Rate equation and conservation of energy equations, modes of heat transfer; Conduction: 1D steady heat conduction with and without heat generation, Unsteady state heat conduction (lumped capacitance method and Heisler chart), heat transfer from extended surfaces; Convection: Governing equations, dimensional analysis, boundary layers, Forced convection - external and internal flows, Natural and mixed convection; Heat Exchanger: Design and types of heat exchangers: Analysis of heat exchanger: LMTD and effectiveness-NTU methods; Radiation: Processes and properties, Black and real body radiation, view factor and radiation exchanges between surfaces in an enclosure; Mass Transfer: Concept of mass transfer.

Course MEL351: Machining and Machine Tools. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Typically offered in semester 5. Course type: core. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Machining and metal cutting (advanced).

MEL351 Machining and Machine Tools — syllabus: Machining as secondary manufacturing processes, types of machining processes, types of cutting tools, Different output characteristics in machining processes; Concept of directrix and generatrix, types of surfaces generated in machining; Determination of material removal rate and machining time in different machining processes; Cutting tool geometry, concepts of master line; Mechanics of chip formation, concept of orthogonal and oblique cutting; Analysis of cutting forces in orthogonal cutting, experimental measurement of cutting force; Cutting temperature: causes, effects, measurement and control; Cutting tool materials, Cutting fluid, tool wear and tool life, role of geometrical and process parameters and cutting fluid on machinability; Machine tools: Types, mechanisms and work holding devices; Grinding: introduction and types of grinding operations, and specifications of grinding wheels.

Course MEP381: Manufacturing and Metrology Lab. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 1.5. Load (L-T-P): 0-0-3. Typically offered in semester 5. Course type: core. Mode: lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Manufacturing and materials (working); Metrology and measurement (working).

MEP381 Manufacturing and Metrology Lab — syllabus: Casting; Metal forming: Rolling, Extrusion, sheet metal forming, forging; Welding: Metal inert gas welding, TIG, gas welding, Spot welding, friction stir welding; Machining: Turning, milling, drilling; Metrology: Coordinate measuring machine, vernier calipers/screw gauge.

Course MEP371: Thermal and Fluid Engineering Lab. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 1.5. Load (L-T-P): 0-0-3. Typically offered in semester 5. Course type: core. Mode: lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Fluid mechanics (working); Heat transfer (working).

MEP371 Thermal and Fluid Engineering Lab — syllabus: Experiments to demonstrate major and minor pipe losses, Bernoulli's principle, Flow regimes, flow measurement devices, performance of turbines, hydraulic/pneumatic systems will be covered under fluid mechanics and machine domain; Whereas experiments to demonstrate different modes of heat transfer (Conduction, Convection and Radiation), and the performance of refrigerator, air conditioner, internal combustion engine will be covered under the domain of thermal engineering.

Course MEL334: Theory of Mechanisms and Machines. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.5. Load (L-T-P): 3-0.5-0. Typically offered in semester 6. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Kinematics of machines (advanced); Balancing and governors (working); Mechanical vibrations (working).

MEL334 Theory of Mechanisms and Machines — syllabus: Kinematics of Mechanisms: Kinematic pairs, diagrams, and inversion; Mobility and range of movement; Displacement, velocity, and acceleration; Analysis of planar linkages; Design of Mechanisms: Dimensional synthesis for motion, path, and function generation; Gears and gear trains; Cam mechanisms, Cam profile synthesis; Dynamics of Machines: Dynamic force analysis; Inertia forces and balancing for rotating and reciprocating machines; Flywheels, Governors; Vibration: Introduction, Single degree of freedom system; Free and forced vibration; Damped, undamped, and overdamped system.

Course MEL304: Applied Numerical Methods. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.5. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-1. Typically offered in semester 6. Course type: core. Mode: lecture-lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: MAL100, MAL101. Skills taught: Numerical methods (advanced); Optimisation (working); Finite element analysis (intro).

MEL304 Applied Numerical Methods — syllabus: Mathematical modelling of some simple engineering problems. Error Analysis: Approximations and round-off errors, Taylor series, truncation errors, error propagations; Root finding techniques: Bracketing Methods-Bisection, False-Position methods; Open Methods-Fixed point, Secant and Newton-Raphson method, Roots of polynomials, rate of convergence.; Linear Algebra: Gauss Elimination, LU Decomposition, Gauss-Seidel.; Optimization: One and Multi-dimensional unconstrained Optimization-Golden, Section search; Optimization: Gradient method, constrained optimization; Curve fitting: Least-squares regression-linear, and polynomial regression; Curve fitting: Interpolation-Lagrange interpolating polynomial, Spline interpolation; Numerical differentiation and integration: Discretization and order to accuracy, Newton-cotes Integration-Trapezoidal, Simpson's rule; Numerical differentiation and integration: Romberg integration; Richardson extrapolation; Methods to solve Ordinary differential equations: Runge-Kutta Method along with its adaptive part, Methods to solve Partial differential equations:

MEL304 Applied Numerical Methods — syllabus: Methods to solve Ordinary differential equations: Runge-Kutta Method along with its adaptive part, Methods to solve Partial differential equations: Finite difference and finite element based methods to solve Elliptic and Parabolic equations; Introduction to Artificial Neural Network.

Course MEP302: Engineering and Machine Drawing. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 2.0. Load (L-T-P): 0-0-4. Typically offered in semester 6. Course type: core. Mode: lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Engineering drawing (advanced); Machine element design (intro).

MEP302 Engineering and Machine Drawing — syllabus: Engineering curves; Theory of projections: 1st and 3rd angle projection, isometric projection; Projection of line, planes, and solids; Projection of section of solids; Development of surfaces; Geometric dimensioning and tolerances: Limits, Fits, tolerances (geometric and dimensional), Tolerance stack up analysis for assembly, concept of production drawing; Keys, cotters and pin joints; Shaft coupling, Gears; 2D assembly drawing.

Course MEP376: Solid Mechanics and Dynamics Lab. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 1.5. Load (L-T-P): 0-0-3. Typically offered in semester 6. Course type: core. Mode: lab. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: MEL232. Co-requisites: MEL334. Skills taught: Mechanical properties of materials (working); Mechanical vibrations (working); Balancing and governors (working).

MEP376 Solid Mechanics and Dynamics Lab — syllabus: Experiments on estimation of material properties: Uni-axial tension test, Uni-axial compression test, Fatigue test, Impact test. Experiments on measurement of stress and strain in structures: Measurement of strain in a cantilever beam using strain gauge and strain amplifier circuit, Measurement of strain for fixed-fixed beam under bending, Measurement of strains under combined bending-torsion loading, Calculation of fringe constant of a material using standard disk under compression test, Estimation of bending stresses in a beam under bending using photoelasticity setup; Experiments on dynamics and vibration of mechanical components/structures: Measurement of natural frequency and estimation of damping properties of different fluids using spring-mass system, Analysis of forced vibration of spring-mass system under base excitation, Measurement of natural frequency for torsional vibration, Static and dynamics balancing of rotating shaft, Design of four-bar mechanism for path/function generation.

Course UGQ301: Interdisciplinary undergraduate project. Offered by Interdisciplinary. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 0-0-6. Typically offered in semester 6. Course type: core. Mode: project. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course NCN100: Practices for Comprehensive wellbeing. Offered by Non-graded core. Typically offered in semester 1. Course type: non-graded. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.
Course LAN103: Professional Ethics. Offered by Liberal Arts. Typically offered in semester 2. Course type: non-graded. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded.

Course MEL414: Internal Combustion Engines. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 2.5-0.5-0. Course type: elective. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Combustion and IC engines (advanced); Power and refrigeration cycles (working).

MEL414 Internal Combustion Engines — syllabus: Introduction: Engine Configurations and components, Engine types and classification, Reciprocating and rotary engines, Valve timing, Thermochemistry of fuel-air mixtures, Engine operative parameters, Torque and power, Efficiencies, Mean effective pressure. Combustion in Spark-ignition Engines: Premixed charge combustion, SI Engine combustion conceptual models, Combustion rate characterization, Thermodynamics analysis of combustion, Flame propagation Phenomenon, Cycle to cycle variation, knocking combustion, Factors affecting Knock. Combustion in Compression-ignition Engines: Fuel injection and spray structure, CI Engine combustion conceptual model, Diesel combustion process characterization, Premixed and mixing controlled combustion, Fuel injection parameters. Engine cooling, lubrication and other systems: Air-cooled Systems, Liquid cooling systems, Function and mechanism of lubrication, Lubrication systems, Exhaust gas recirculation, Variable valve timing. Formation of Engine emissions:

MEL414 Internal Combustion Engines — syllabus: systems, Function and mechanism of lubrication, Lubrication systems, Exhaust gas recirculation, Variable valve timing. Formation of Engine emissions: Sources of engine emissions, Formation of carbon monoxide, NOx Formation, Unburned hydrocarbon emissions, Soot and particulate formation, Emission Measurement. Exhaust Aftertreatment devices: Basics of catalytic exhaust treatment, Three-way catalytic converter, Diesel oxidation catalyst, Diesel Particulate filter, Regeneration, Gasoline particulate filter, NOx absorber, Selective catalytic converter.

Course MEL416: Power Plant Engineering. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 2-1-0. Course type: elective. Mode: lecture-tutorial. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: MEL211. Skills taught: Power and refrigeration cycles (advanced); Turbomachinery (working).

MEL416 Power Plant Engineering — syllabus: Economics of Power Generation: Introduction, Power plant economics, Types of power plants. Steam Power Plants: Economics of Power Generation, Reheating and regeneration, Feedwater heaters, Supercritical pressure cycle, Deaerator, Binary vapour cycle, Combined cycle plants, Coal, Coal analysis, Combustion reactions, Energy balance of steam generator. Steam Generators, Steam Turbines, Condenser: Basic types of steam generators, Fire tube and water tube boilers, Ash handling system, Feedwater treatment, Steam turbines, Condenser, Cooling towers. Diesel Engine and Gas Turbine Power Plants: Combustion in a CI engine, Performance characteristics, Supercharging, Layout of a diesel engine power plant, Gas turbine power plant, Components of gas turbine plant, gas turbine fuels, Gas turbine Materials. Nuclear and Hydroelectric Power Plants: Nuclear fusion and fission, Chain reaction, Nuclear fuels, Components of nuclear reactor, Classification of reactors, Nuclear waste and its disposal, Hydroelectric power plant classification, Pelton, Francis and Kaplan turbines.

MEL416 Power Plant Engineering — syllabus: reactor, Classification of reactors, Nuclear waste and its disposal, Hydroelectric power plant classification, Pelton, Francis and Kaplan turbines. Non-conventional and Renewable Power Generation: Renewable energy sources potential, Solar power plants, Thermal energy, Wind energy, Wind power plant, Waste to power generation, Geothermal energy.

Course MEL501: Advanced Engineering Mathematics. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Course type: elective. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Numerical methods (working).
MEL501 Advanced Engineering Mathematics — syllabus: Ordinary Differential equations: Review of 2nd and Higher order ODEs, Systems of ODEs, Series solutions.

Course MEL554: Non-Conventional Machining Processes. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Course type: elective. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Machining and metal cutting (advanced).

MEL554 Non-Conventional Machining Processes — syllabus: Introduction to non-conventional machining, classification of non-conventional machining processes. Electro-Discharge Machining (EDM), process mechanism of material removal, parameters affecting EDM and application. Traveling Wire EDM. Electrochemical Machining (ECM), Mechanism of material removal, Tool design, Parameters affecting ECM, Applications. Electro-chemical Honing (ECH), Electrochemical Deburring (ECD), Chemical Machining. Ultrasonic Machining, Cutting Tool System Design, Mechanism of cutting, Parameters affecting USM applications. Abrasive Jet Machining, Variables of AJM, Nozzle Design, Water Jet Machining (WJM), Abrasive Water Jet Machining (AWJM). Hybrid Machining Processes: Grinding, Electrical Discharge Grinding, Electrochemical Grinding, Electrochemical Discharge Grinding. Introduction to Micromachining: Size effect, challenges in micro-scale material removal. Laser Beam Machining, Thermal and Non-thermal analysis, and applications. Electron Beam Machining and Ion Beam Machining: Mechanism, process parameters and applications.

MEL554 Non-Conventional Machining Processes — syllabus: Thermal and Non-thermal analysis, and applications. Electron Beam Machining and Ion Beam Machining: Mechanism, process parameters and applications. Plasma arc machining, applications, Plasma arc surfacing.

Course MEL558: Surface Engineering. Offered by Mechanical Engineering. Credits: 3.0. Load (L-T-P): 3-0-0. Course type: elective. Mode: lecture. Programme: B.Tech Mechanical Engineering. Hard prerequisites: none recorded. Skills taught: Materials science (advanced); Heat treatment (working).

MEL558 Surface Engineering — syllabus: Introduction to surface engineering - Concept and Importance. Surface Degradation: Causes, types and consequences of surface degradation. Classification of surface modification techniques, advantages and their limitations. Materials for Surface Engineering: Selection of materials for engineering the surfaces for specific applications, structure and property relationship of coatings system. Conventional surface engineering and heat treatment practices. Surface modification of ferrous and non-ferrous materials like nitriding, cyaniding, aluminizing etc. Techniques of thin film coatings; Vapour deposition processes: Chemical Vapour Deposition of different types of coatings. Vacuum Evaporation Deposition, Cathodic Arc Evaporation Deposition, sputtering and its advancements. Thermal Spraying methods: Classifications, Flame and plasma spraying, HVOF, cold spray techniques and its variants. Electroplating, Electroless coating, laser, Electron beam and Microwave assisted Surface Engineering, Friction Surfacing and Friction stir processing. Physical Characterization:

MEL558 Surface Engineering — syllabus: coating, laser, Electron beam and Microwave assisted Surface Engineering, Friction Surfacing and Friction stir processing. Physical Characterization: Microstructure, Surface morphology, Phase analysis, Determination of Crystallite size in coatings. Mechanical Characterization: Determination of thickness of coating, coating hardness, Adhesion of surface coating, Surface roughness. Performance evaluation of coating: Friction and wear performance, Evaluation of corrosion resistance, Assessment of oxidation resistance, Applications of tribological coatings.

[probation] If SGPA falls below 4.5, he/she will be put on academic probation and intimation has to be sent by the academic office to the department where the student is registered. He/she will be allowed to register for the next semester only if CGPA is greater than or equal to 4.0. (limit: 4.5 SGPA (threshold)) [clause 2.3.6 (a)]

[probation] If, in the subsequent semesters, CGPA is greater than or equal to 4.0 but less than 4.5, he/she will be put on academic probation. [termination] A student will normally not be allowed to register and program will be auto terminated if his/her CGPA falls below 4.0, or his/her CGPA falls below 4.5 for three consecutive semesters. (limit: 4.0 CGPA (minimum)) [clause 2.3.6 (d)]

[audit] A student has the option of auditing upto 3 credits in a semester with consent from the course instructor(s). Grades obtained in audit courses are not counted for computing SGPA/CGPA although the grade earned by the student is reflected in the grade card or transcript. However, a pass grade (other than F grade) is essential for completing an audit course. (limit: 3.0 credits per semester) [clause 2.3.1]

[credit_validity] The credits earned for the course or thesis are valid for up to seven years only (irrespective of whether the student was on leave or not) and shall not be counted towards the requirements of the degree if they are acquired earlier than seven years or more. [grade_improvement] A student is allowed to improve his/her grade (other than F) by repeating the course or replacing it with another course if it is an elective course. (limit: 3.0 courses (maximum, entire programme)) [clause 2.3.5]

[honours] A student at the end of 5th semester can register for BTech Honours (Course based/Thesis based) depending on their academic performance, interest, and evaluation. Open learning resource: Engineering Mechanics. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Guwahati. Instructor: Dr. G. Saravana Kumar; Prof. U.S. Dixit. Format: syllabus PDF + video course. Duration: not stated by the provider. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA. Supports: Statics and equilibrium, Free body diagrams, Truss and frame analysis, Friction and its applications, Rigid body dynamics. Statics including forces, moments, equilibrium and free body diagrams; analysis of trusses, frames, machines, beams and cables; friction; centroids and moments of inertia; virtual work and energy methods; particle and rigid-body dynamics; an introduction to vibration.

Open learning resource: Dynamics of Machines. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Kanpur. Instructor: Prof. Amitabha Ghosh. Format: syllabus PDF + video course. Approximate duration: 45.0 hours. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA. Supports: Rigid body dynamics, Balancing and governors, Mechanical vibrations, Kinematics of machines. Machine dynamics including rigid-body motion, gyroscopic effects, balancing of rotating bodies and engine unbalance; speed control through flywheels and governors; vibration theory for single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems, forced and damped vibration, and approximate methods for natural frequencies.

Open learning resource: Design of Machine Elements. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Kharagpur. Instructor: Prof. B. Maiti; Prof. G. Chakraborty; Prof. S.K. Roychowdhury. Format: syllabus PDF + video course. Duration: not stated by the provider. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA. Supports: Machine element design, Stress and strain analysis, Failure theories and fatigue. Design philosophy, materials, and the stress and strain analysis behind mechanical components, including failure theories and fatigue; applied to fasteners, keys, couplings, springs, levers, brackets, shafts, and thin and thick cylinders.

Open learning resource: Fundamentals of Manufacturing Processes. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Roorkee. Instructor: Prof. D.K. Dwivedi; Prof. Shamik Basak. Format: syllabus PDF + online course. Approximate duration: 12.0 weeks. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA. Supports: Casting processes, Metal forming, Welding and joining, Machining and metal cutting, Heat treatment. Manufacturing concepts, process selection and break-even analysis; casting, metal forming, joining, machining and grinding; heat treatment of steel and aluminium alloys; methods for improving surface properties including surface modification, composition changes and coatings.

Open learning resource: Principles of Physical Metallurgy. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Kharagpur. Instructor: Prof. R.N. Ghosh. Format: syllabus PDF + web course. Approximate duration: 44.0 hours. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA. Supports: Phase diagrams and transformations, Crystal structure and defects, Heat treatment, Mechanical properties of materials. How microstructures form in metals and alloys during processing and how they relate to in-service properties; thermodynamics and kinetics of phase transformations; alloy design, casting, forming and heat treatment; structure-property relationships; examination tools, crystal structure and crystal defects.

Open learning resource: Applied Thermodynamics. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Guwahati. Instructor: Prof. Niranjan Sahoo; Prof. Pranab K. Mondal. Format: syllabus PDF + online course. Thermodynamic foundations and cycles used in power and refrigeration systems: steam and gas power cycles, refrigeration, psychrometrics, internal combustion engines, and gas turbine and aircraft/rocket propulsion cycles, with a review of basic thermodynamics.

Open learning resource: Heat and Mass Transfer. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Bombay. Instructor: Prof. S.P. Sukhatme; Prof. U.N. Gaitonde. Format: syllabus PDF + video course. Fundamentals of heat transfer: steady, transient and numerical conduction; radiation; forced and natural convection; heat exchangers; condensation and boiling; and mass transfer including its analogy with heat transfer.

Open learning resource: Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering. Provider: NPTEL. Host institute: IIT Madras. Instructor: Dr. Ranjit Bauri. Format: syllabus PDF + web course.
